questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (2F-G)$ at the point $(0,-1,2)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)={e}^{x}\,i+yz\,j,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=z\,i+(x+2y)\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F-G) & =∇\times (2F)+∇\times (-G) \\  & =2∇\times F-∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ {e}^{x} & yz & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(0)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(yz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(0)-\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{x})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(yz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x})]k \\  & =(0-y)i-(0-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-y\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F-G) & =2∇\times F-∇\times G \\  & =2[-y\,i]-[z\,i+(x+2y)\,k] \\  & =-2y\,i-z\,i-(x+2y)\,k \\  & =-(2y+z)\,i-(x+2y)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,-1,2),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (2F-G))(0,-1,2) & =-(2(-1)+2)\,i-(0+2(-1))\,k \\  & =-(-2+2)\,i-(0-2)\,k \\  & =2\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F-3G)$ at the point $(1,0,9)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=(2\sqrt{z}+x)\,i+xy\,j+{y}^{2}\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=3{x}^{2}y\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-3G) & =∇\times F+∇\times (-3G) \\  & =∇\times F-3∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ 2\sqrt{z}+x & xy & {y}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(2\sqrt{z}+x)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\sqrt{z}+x)]k \\  & =(2y-0)i-(0-\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}})j+(y-0)k \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-3G) & =∇\times F-3∇\times G \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y\,k-3[3{x}^{2}y\,k] \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y\,k-9{x}^{2}y\,k \\  & =2y\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,j+y(1-9{x}^{2})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(1,0,9),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-3G))(1,0,9) & =2(0)\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{9}}\,j+0(1-9(1)^{2})\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F+3G)$ at the point $(0,1,-2)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)={y}^{2}\,i+z\,j+{x}^{2}\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=-3{x}^{2}\,j-k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+3G) & =∇\times F+∇\times (3G) \\  & =∇\times F+3∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ {y}^{2} & z & {x}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}({y}^{2})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})]k \\  & =(0-1)i-(2x-0)j+(0-2y)k \\  & =-i-2x\,j-2y\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+3G) & =∇\times F+3∇\times G \\  & =-i-2x\,j-2y\,k+3[-3{x}^{2}\,j-k] \\  & =-i-2x\,j-2y\,k-9{x}^{2}\,j-3k \\  & =-i-(9{x}^{2}+2x)\,j-(2y+3)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,1,-2),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F+3G))(0,1,-2) & =-i-(9(0)^{2}+2(0))\,j-(2(1)+3)\,k \\  & =-i-5\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨0,x,2\sqrt{y}⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=y{z}^{2}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}},0,1⟩,\,∇f=⟨0,{z}^{2},2yz⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(0,4,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & {z}^{2} & 2yz \\ 0 & x & 2\sqrt{y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[({z}^{2})(2\sqrt{y})-(x)(2yz)]i-[(0)(2\sqrt{y})-(0)(2yz)]j+[(0)(x)-(0)({z}^{2})]k \\  & =(2{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}-2xyz)\,i+0\,j+0\,k \\  & =⟨2{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}-2xyz,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(y{z}^{2})⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}},0,1⟩+⟨2{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}-2xyz,0,0⟩ \\  & =⟨{z}^{2}\sqrt{y},0,y{z}^{2}⟩+⟨2{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}-2xyz,0,0⟩ \\  & =⟨3{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}-2xyz,0,y{z}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
∇\times (f\,F)(0,4,1)=⟨6,0,4⟩.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x{e}^{y},yz,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=x{e}^{-y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨-y,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩,\,∇f=⟨{e}^{-y},-x{e}^{-y},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(0,1,2).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {e}^{-y} & -x{e}^{-y} & 0 \\ x{e}^{y} & yz & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[(-x{e}^{-y})(0)-(yz)(0)]i-[({e}^{-y})(0)-(x{e}^{y})(0)]j+[({e}^{-y})(yz)-(x{e}^{y})(-x{e}^{-y})]k \\  & =0\,i+0j+(yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2})k \\  & =⟨0,0,yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x{e}^{-y})⟨-y,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-xy{e}^{-y},0,-{x}^{2}⟩+⟨0,0,yz{e}^{-y}+{x}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-xy{e}^{-y},0,yz{e}^{-y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
∇\times (f\,F)(0,1,2)=⟨0,0,\frac{2}{e}⟩.
$$
